questions.question: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. _TUVTR_WU_UXVN_Y
questions.questionHtml:
Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series.

_TUVTR_WU_UXVN_Y
questions.solution:
The final series becomes:
STUV TRUW UPUX VNUY

1st Letter: S → T → U → V Pattern: Each increases by +1 alphabetically.

2nd Letter: T → R → P → N Pattern: Each decreases by -2 alphabetically.

3rd Letter: U → U → U → U Pattern: Constant letter 'U'.

4th Letter: V → W → X → Y Pattern: Each increases by +1 alphabetically.

questions.solution:

Engineers are not necessarily all men, nor all fathers → so Engineers will partly overlap with Men.

Some Engineers may also be Fathers (intersection of all three).

questions.question: You are a sincere SSC aspirant and this examination is extremely important for you as it is your last attempt, but this year you are facing several difficulties as the admit card was released very late leaving you with little time for travel, your centre is 600–700 km away, there is severe mismanagement at the venue with delay in start, poor facilities, low-quality rough sheets and pens, students who complain are threatened by bouncers, and you even hear rumours of remote access and unfair practices; in this situation, as an honest and serious candidate, what will be the most appropriate action?
questions.questionHtml: You are a sincere SSC aspirant and this examination is extremely important for you as it is your last attempt, but this year you are facing several difficulties as the admit card was released very late leaving you with little time for travel, your centre is 600–700 km away, there is severe mismanagement at the venue with delay in start, poor facilities, low-quality rough sheets and pens, students who complain are threatened by bouncers, and you even hear rumours of remote access and unfair practices; in this situation, as an honest and serious candidate, what will be the most appropriate action?

options.text: Remain quiet and give the exam ignoring everything.
options.html: Remain quiet and give the exam ignoring everything.

options.text: Create a scene at the centre and protest against the authorities.
options.html: Create a scene at the centre and protest against the authorities.

options.text: Appear in the exam sincerely, collect valid evidence of mismanagement, and later raise a complaint through proper channels.
options.html: Appear in the exam sincerely, collect valid evidence of mismanagement, and later raise a complaint through proper channels.

options.text: Leave the exam midway in frustration, thinking everything is useless.
options.html: Leave the exam midway in frustration, thinking everything is useless.

questions.solution:
Explanation:

Option (a): Ignoring everything and just giving the exam is not the best choice because although you appear for the exam, the issues remain unreported and no action is taken.

Option (b): Creating a scene or protesting at the centre is not appropriate because it may lead to disciplinary action against you and also disturb your chances in the exam.

Option (d): Leaving the exam midway is the worst reaction because it will waste your last attempt and your years of preparation.

Option (c): This is the most logical action — you should remain calm, appear in the exam sincerely so that your attempt is not wasted, and later raise your concerns properly by collecting evidence and reporting through RTI, social media, or directly to SSC. This way, both your exam and your voice are protected.

questions.question: In a row of 41 students facing North, A is 12th from the left end and B is 18th from the right end. If C is exactly between A and B, then what is C’s position from the left end?
questions.questionHtml: In a row of 41 students facing North, A is 12th from the left end and B is 18th from the right end. If C is exactly between A and B, then what is C’s position from the left end?
questions.solution:
Solution:

Total students = 41

Position of A from left = 12

Position of B from right = 18 → From left = 41 – 18 + 1 = 24

So, A = 12th, B = 24th

Midpoint = (12 + 24) ÷ 2 = 18

questions.question: You are a final-year student who has been preparing sincerely for SSC exams for the past 3 years. Just two days before your exam, you get a job offer letter from a private company with a decent salary but less job security. On the other hand, SSC exam is very important for you, but you are not fully confident about your preparation this year. In this situation, what will be the most appropriate step you should take?
questions.questionHtml:
You are a final-year student who has been preparing sincerely for SSC exams for the past 3 years. Just two days before your exam, you get a job offer letter from a private company with a decent salary but less job security. On the other hand, SSC exam is very important for you, but you are not fully confident about your preparation this year.

In this situation, what will be the most appropriate step you should take?

options.text: Immediately join the private company and forget about SSC.
options.html: Immediately join the private company and forget about SSC.

options.text: Reject the company offer and take the SSC exam with full focus.
options.html: Reject the company offer and take the SSC exam with full focus.

options.text: Join the company for safety, but still appear for the SSC exam.
options.html: Join the company for safety, but still appear for the SSC exam.

options.text: Leave both opportunities and prepare again for next year with a fresh mind.
options.html: Leave both opportunities and prepare again for next year with a fresh mind.

questions.solution:
Solution:
The most appropriate answer is (c) Join the company for safety, but still appear for the SSC exam.

Thus, the best balanced approach is to secure the private job but still attempt SSC, as success in SSC would give long-term stability.
